title: Who Moved the Frontier? Paying Open Frontier Challenges with Free Identities
abstract: arXiv:2611.14974v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: In an open frontier challenge, anyone, person or AI agent, submits changes to a shared problem, and a change that beats the best measured score becomes the public baseline. How should it pay when identities are free? Rank prizes can be gamed: on a replay of one track of a recent challenge, one solver's steps under two identities would have taken first and second prize. We consider a prediction-market rule, proposed for machine-learning contests, that pays each accepted step for the progress it adds; with exact scores, among rules that see only a step's start and end, only these resist splitting and merging, and extra identities gain nothing. With noisy scores and independent normal runs, we prove that any payment that never takes money back and pays real improvements also pays something, on average, to a change that does nothing. We propose a fee per submission, at least what luck pays per attempt, that removes each attempt's expected

translated_title: 谁动了前沿？当身份免费时如何为开放前沿挑战付费
translated_abstract: 在开放前沿挑战中，任何人或AI智能体都可以向一个共享问题提交更改，凡是超越当前最佳测量分数的更改即成为公开基线。当身份免费时，应当如何支付奖励？基于排名的奖金是可能被操纵的：在重现近期某挑战一个赛道的实验中，一名求解者仅用两个身份提交的步骤就能同时斩获第一名和第二名。我们研究了一种为机器学习竞赛提出的预测市场规则，它按每个被接受步骤所增添的进展来支付；在分数精确的情形下，在那些只能观察到步骤起点和终点的规则之中，唯有这类规则能够抵抗拆分与合并操纵，且多余的身份不会带来任何收益。在分数含噪且各次运行为独立正态分布的条件下，我们证明：任何从不收回资金、只对真实改进付费的支付机制，平均而言也会向一个毫无实际改变的提交支付一定金额。为此我们提出对每次提交收取费用——至少等于运气在每次尝试中的期望所得——以消除每次尝试的期望（收益）。（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 论文指出开放前沿挑战中的排名奖金可被多免费身份操纵，提出按每个提交所新增进展付费的预测市场支付规则——在精确分数下是唯一能抵御拆分与合并操纵且使额外身份无利可图的机制，并对每次提交收费以消除噪声分数带来的运气期望收益。
en_tdlr: The paper shows that rank prizes in open frontier challenges can be gamed with multiple free identities, proposes a prediction-market rule paying each submission for its added progress—which uniquely resists splitting and merging under exact scores—and introduces a per-submission fee to remove the expected gains that luck earns under noisy scores.
